name: China

demographics.notes: World's second-most populous nation; entering a structural demographic transition with a rapidly aging populace and contracting working-age labor force following the historical One-Child policy.

economy.notes: World's second-largest economy by nominal GDP and largest by Purchasing Power Parity (PPP); global manufacturing powerhouse producing ~30% of global industrial output, dominating electric vehicles, renewable energy, and shipbuilding.
major_exports: Electric vehicles, lithium-ion batteries, and solar PV cells (The 'New Three')
Industrial machinery, heavy electrical apparatus, and robotics
Steel, refined metals, and chemical precursors
Commercial cargo vessels and bulk carriers
major_imports: Crude petroleum, natural gas, and coal
Iron ore, copper concentrate, and unrefined bauxite

military.defence_spending_pct_gdp_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS), 2024 data, extracted from user-provided dataset (file last updated 2026-02-24)
military.arms_exports_source: World Bank WDI (MS.MIL.XPRT.KD), constant USD, from user-provided dataset
key_equipment_or_doctrines: Anti-Access/Area Denial (A2/AD): Multi-layered missile and sensor architecture designed to deny US carrier strike groups access within the First and Second Island Chains
PLA Rocket Force: DF-17 hypersonic glide vehicles, DF-21D/DF-26 anti-ship ballistic missiles ('Carrier Killers'), and DF-41 solid-fuel road-mobile/silo ICBMs
PLA Navy: Numerically world's largest navy (>370 hulls), operating Fujian CATOBAR aircraft carrier, Type 055 Renhai stealth guided-missile cruisers, and Type 094 nuclear ballistic missile submarines
PLA Air Force: 5th-generation J-20 'Mighty Dragon' stealth air superiority fighters, J-16 strike aircraft, and Y-20 strategic airlifters
Theater Command Structure: Integrated joint warfighting commands (Eastern Theater focused on Taiwan/East China Sea; Western Theater focused on Sino-Indian LAC)

primary_sources: Coal (56% of total energy consumption - backbone of domestic baseload electricity generation)
Crude oil (19% - over 70% imported via seaborne tankers)
Hydropower, solar, and wind (16% - world's largest installed renewable energy capacity)
Natural gas (8% - domestic production plus pipeline imports from Russia/Central Asia and LNG)
Nuclear power (3% - fastest-growing civil nuclear reactor buildout globally)
energy.note: World's largest energy consumer and crude oil importer; aggressively building overland pipeline networks (Power of Siberia, Central Asia-China pipeline) and expanding domestic renewables to mitigate maritime chokepoint exposure.

major_ports: Port of Shanghai (World's #1 busiest container port, handling >47 million TEUs annually)
Port of Ningbo-Zhoushan (World's #1 port by total cargo tonnage, handling >1.3 billion metric tons)
Port of Shenzhen & Guangzhou (Pearl River Delta global manufacturing export gateways)
Port of Qingdao & Tianjin (Heavy industrial, energy, and iron ore import hubs in northern China)
strategic_airports: Beijing Capital & Beijing Daxing International (PEK / PKX)
Shanghai Pudong International Airport (PVG - major global air cargo hub)
infrastructure.energy_grid_resilience: State Grid Corporation of China operates the world's most advanced Ultra-High Voltage (UHV) DC transmission network, transmitting massive hydro and solar power from western provinces over 3,000 km to eastern industrial coastal metros.
infrastructure.digital_infrastructure: World's most extensive 5G network (>3.5M base stations); sovereign BeiDou-3 global satellite navigation constellation; leading domestic supercomputing centers and sovereign hyperscale cloud clusters.

top_partners: ASEAN (largest regional trading partner, central to intermediate manufacturing integration)
European Union (primary export destination for consumer goods, green tech, and industrial components)
United States (crucial export market, subject to tariffs and strategic export control competition)
Russia (strategic partner for discounted crude oil, natural gas, coal, and fertilizer imports)
Japan & South Korea (critical suppliers of high-end machinery, display panels, and electronic components)
chokepoint_exposure: Strait of Malacca ('Malacca Dilemma' — ~80% of imported crude oil must transit this narrow chokepoint)
First Island Chain straits (Miyako Strait, Bashi Channel — strategic naval bottlenecks monitored by US and allied forces)
Strait of Hormuz (over 40% of imported crude originates in Gulf producers)

core_competencies: Global monopoly on rare earth permanent magnet refining (>90% of global capacity) and critical mineral processing (lithium, cobalt, graphite)
World-leading commercial and industrial battery manufacturing (CATL and BYD control over 50% of world EV batteries)
Advanced 5G/6G telecommunications infrastructure, high-voltage electrical grid technology, and high-speed rail engineering
Hypersonic glide aerodynamics, quantum satellite encryption, and artificial intelligence computer vision
tech_vulnerabilities: Vulnerability to advanced semiconductor equipment embargoes (EUV photolithography tools from ASML, advanced deposition/etch tools from US/Japan)
Dependence on US-origin Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software for leading-edge chip design
Import reliance on commercial aviation jet engines (CFM LEAP engines for the COMAC C919 airliner)

land_borders: India (3488 km along the disputed Line of Actual Control)
Afghanistan (91 km via the Wakhan Corridor)

politics.system: Unitary socialist one-party republic under the leadership of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP)
politics.executive: General Secretary of the CCP, President of the PRC, and Chairman of the Central Military Commission (concentrated in Xi Jinping). Premier of the State Council leads government administration.
politics.legislature: National People's Congress (NPC), the 2,980-member unicameral national legislature; Standing Committee of the NPC exercises legislative power year-round.
politics.judiciary: Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate, constitutionally subordinate to the National People's Congress and guided by Party leadership.

nuclear.delivery_systems: Rapidly expanding operational nuclear triad: Road-mobile and silo-based ICBMs (DF-41, DF-31AG, DF-5B), submarine-launched ballistic missiles (JL-2 and JL-3 deployed on Type 094 SSBNs), and air-launched dual-capable ballistic missiles (H-6N bombers).
nuclear.notes: Estimated ~500 operational nuclear warheads (SIPRI / US DoD 2024), projected to reach 1,000+ by 2030. Maintains a declared No-First-Use (NFU) policy, while constructing extensive hardened silo fields in Yumen, Hami, and Ordos.

strategic_priorities: Achieving national reunification with Taiwan and deterring foreign military intervention across the First Island Chain
Attaining complete technological self-reliance ('Choke Point' indigenous substitution) in semiconductors, AI, and industrial equipment
Consolidating the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) and developing alternative continental logistics corridors to bypass maritime chokepoints
Strengthening the comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination with Russia to counter Western containment and promote a multipolar world order
Securing regional maritime dominance in the South China Sea and expanding blue-water naval power into the Indian Ocean
dependencies: Energy security: Imports over 70% of crude oil and over 40% of natural gas, predominantly via vulnerable sea lines of communication
High-end semiconductor lithography and design tool ecosystem reliant on Western and Japanese supply chains
Critical bulk agricultural imports (soybeans and feed grains from the US, Brazil, and Argentina) to sustain national food supply
Reliance on the US dollar-denominated global financial clearing system (SWIFT) for international trade settlements
vulnerabilities: The 'Malacca Dilemma': Roughly 80% of seaborne crude oil imports transit the narrow Strait of Malacca, an arterial bottleneck outside PLA defense umbrellas
Rapid demographic aging: Shrinking fertility and workforce contraction placing unprecedented fiscal demands on pensions and healthcare while reducing economic dynamism
Real estate sector restructuring: Protracted downturn in residential property development and high local government financing vehicle (LGFV) debt overhang
Intensifying multilateral encirclement: Coordinated export controls, defense pacts, and tech restrictions by the US, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and European allies
strengths: Unrivalled industrial base: The only nation possessing every industrial category under the UN classification; world's undisputed workshop across steel, electronics, chemicals, and green technologies
Colossal shipbuilding and naval capacity: Commands over 50% of world commercial shipbuilding tonnage and rapid naval construction capacity exceeding all Western shipyards combined
Dominance in critical green transition supply chains: Monopolizes over 75% of global solar supply chains, 70% of EV battery cells, and 90% of refined rare earth magnets
Vast sovereign foreign exchange reserves ($3.2T+) and deep domestic state-backed capital allocation mechanisms
